A Loud Sound Just Shut Down a Bank's Data Center for 10 Hours

"There is still very little known about how sound can cause hard drive failure"

Really? How about /literally shaking the running drive/. Why that will break it should be obvious.

And this is why you test things and have redundant failovers in place.

Really the only things I think they did wrong here was (a) having their backup site offline when it should have been ready to take over if anything went wrong, and (b) not running the test on the backup site first before running it on their main, in-use data center. Now that I think of it, maybe (c) not running the test at 3am on a Tuesday morning or somesuch time when usage would be lower.
Back around 99 I worked for PB/NEC. Had customers screaming all the time-after putting their tower on subwoofer bass boxes.

Interesting ... I've been an 'amatuer' computer hardware guy forever, since way back, even before 286's builds I did, and never realized this sound/HDD problem existed, which made the article interesting to me. Nice to know, something I never considered.

Simple "centripetal force". The plates spin, as they do they attempt to maintain the same plane they spun at. While the drive is in full use, simply turning the tower over can destroy it. The readers are a tiny distance from the plates themselves. As vibrations (or full tilt) happen, they strike the platters.
Cool, thanks for the info ... again, I knew of the sensitivity, just didn't realize the sound (or ever really thought about it).
